recipes.name: Chocolate Mint Candies Cookies
ingredients_raw: 3 (4.5 ounce) packages chocolate covered thin mints

steps.text: In a saucepan over medium heat, cook the sugar, butter and water, stirring occasionally until melted. Remove from heat, stir in the chocolate chips until melted and set aside to cool for 10 minutes.

Pour the chocolate mixture into a large bowl, and beat in the eggs, one at a time. Combine the flour, baking soda and salt, stir into the chocolate mixture. Cover and refrigerate dough for at least 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease cookie sheets. Roll cookie dough into walnut sized balls and place 2 inches apart onto the prepared cookie sheets.

Bake for 8 to 10 minutes in the preheated oven, be careful not to overbake. When cookies come out of the oven, Press one mint wafer into the top of each cookie and let sit for 1 minute. When the mint is softened, swirl with the back of a spoon or toothpick to make a pattern with the green filling of the mint wafer. For smaller cookies, break mints in half.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate Mint Candies Cookies
raw_recipe.description: I received this recipe through a cookie exchange years ago, and it has become a favorite of family and friends.

video.description: In this video, you’ll see how to use thin chocolate mint candies to make unforgettable holiday cookies. The cookies are slightly underbaked, allowing the mints to be pressed into them while they are still warm. As the candies melt, the cookie becomes rich and minty.

review.reviewBody:
These cookies are the best cookies I have baked to date so far. I have baked this cookie three times and there are a couple tricky techniques to make this cookie completely out of this world. 

First, it really makes a HUGE difference on the amount of grease you spread on the pan. More grease means the sides will bake quicker than the structural integrity of the cookie. I spayed the cookie sheet with Pam and then wiped excess off with a paper towel. This did the trick.

Second is the time and placement of the Andes mint chocolate. I admit I did have trouble trying to figure this one out. The solution is you first let the cookie cool about a minute or until the cookie looks pretty deflated. Second, you place the mint on top (logo facing down) and press it into the cookie. Try only on a few until you start to get a hang of it. Then when the sides look shiny, but the middle still have a flat surface. Take a teaspoon and lightly flip the mint. Then drag the mint on the inner rim of the cookie. After the cookies have finished their decorative process. Promptly place them in the refrigerator still on the tray. Placing them on a cooling rack only delays the initial chocolate hardening. 

Well I hope this review and these key tricks helped. Happy Baking!!

A few changes. I found the green swirl on the top in the photos to be almost invisible and (since the recipe says it makes 36 cookies) I bought a box of 36 Fanny May Mint Meltaway Candies from Amazon instead of Andes Thin Mints. 18 of them have a chocolate brown coating, and 18 of them have a pastel green coating. I substituted 1 cup of the recipe's chocolate chips with the 18 brown-coated candies for melting, and cut the 18 green-coated candies in half, diagonally (corner-to-corner). After making the dough, I divided it in half and rolled each into a flat-ended "log" which I wrapped in plastic wrap and set on a plate to chill in the fridge (2 hours). Each log was unwrapped and cut into 18 equal chunks with a bench knife, then each chunk was rolled into a ball and baked as directed (8-1/2 minutes, but on Silpat mat-lined baking sheets). When the cookies came out of the oven, I let them sit on the baking sheet for 1 minute, then pressed a half-piece of candy, cut-side-down, onto the center of each cookie, so there was a pale green piece of candy on each cookie. I left each candy half-cube as is, no swirling, and cooled them on a baking rack. Perfect, scrumptious, and rather pretty as well.

As usual I read the reviews before starting - I have to say the advice was spot on. The helpful tips were - 1- make sure the dough is very cold before you start (it's almost fudge-like). 2- Parchment paper instead of greasing your pan. 3- Half an Andes mint on each cookie about 1 minute after you remove them from the oven, and then go right back and flip the unmelted mint over. This was the hardest part, to get that swirly mint look. Mine cooked for 9 1/2 minutes - they are EXCELLENT. This is a keeper for sure.

Love these at holiday time! I’ve made them a number of times and never had an issue. Just be sure to follow the directions and let the chocolate mixture cool a little before you add eggs or they will cook before fully incorporated. Add 1/2 or 1 tsp peppermint extract if you really love the peppermint. Place on parchment paper to bake. I make small cookies using a small cookie scoop. They spread and are flat so small looks best, then just add 1/2 of a candy on each one. Bite size and great addition to a cookie platter, they also freeze well.

I make double this recipe every year for the holidays. They are the best cookie I have ever had! Fudge AND chocolate mints??!? YES MAMA PLEASE! After years of making, I have never tweaked the ingredients* and they always get rave compliments. HOWEVER, there is one major time-saving improvement that desperately needs to be made to the instructions, in my opinion. Gone are my hours and hours in the kitchen cursing and ruining my wrists trying to get the stiff dough to work using these instructions. This year, I finally figured out how make them in less than half the time they used to take me. BETWEEN STEPS 2 AND 3 - YOU WILL NEED A COOKIE SCOOPER. Cover and refrigerate for a couple hours (until the outside of the dough starts to set). Scoop firmer parts of dough into balls using cookie scooper and put the balls back into the fridge until ready to bake (overnight is OK). If, while scooping, parts of the dough towards the center do not hold their shape as they are still warm, leave them to firm another hour or two and then repeat scooping. * Although I have successfully substituted out regular chocolate for people who don't like mint. This year I'll be trying reese's minis! I have also made my own mint chocolates by: (a) carefully melting chocolate chips in a bain marie on the stove; (b) when the mixture is free of clumps, add mint extract and stir; (c) pour out onto parchment paper into large square and spread to approx 1/8 inch thick; (d) when fully cooled, cut into chunks resembling the shape of andes mints.

This cookie was terrific! I used the exact ingredients listed in the recipe (using Andes candies) and it was delicious. In order to ensure that the dough was adequately cooled, I chilled the balls of cookie dough on a cookie sheet in the refrigerator prior to baking. Also, since I was using a dark cookie sheet, I lowered the oven temp to 325. Lastly, after my first sheet of cookies, I decided to use parchment paper. I would absolutely make these again!

I have made this cookie for 25+ years. When I got the recipe from a lady who was a very experienced baker who would provide her product for catered events, the instructions said to line your baking sheet with aluminum foil - do not grease. The key is to make the ball a little smaller than 1 inch and bake them no more than 10 minutes!!!! They appear very soft but they remain chewy. Also, put only 1/2 a mint on top. Let sit for a bit so the chocolate softens and swirl with the back of the spoon.

I really think the key is a foil lined sheet! It has worked for 25 years so far and then your cookie is not greasy at all.

Made 1/2 of this recipe as a trial run. My package of mint baking chips were chocolate, white and green. I used the chocolate and white for the batter and melted the green mint chips along with 1 teaspoon of shortening and piped on top of the melted, swirled mint patties. These are so easy to make and have a delicious minty, chocolate flavor. I only baked for 7 minutes on parchment lined cookie sheets. I can't wait to make for our upcoming St. Patrick's Day party. Thanks for sharing your 5 star recipe, Jackie Schmidt!

Delicious cookies. I used a 10 oz bag of ghiradelli bittersweet chips and they were plenty chocolatey! No need for the full 16 oz. I also used 1.5 cups all purpose flour and 1 cup bread flour because I ran out of all purpose flour. Refrigerated for about 6 hours and it really wasn’t necessary — some cookie doughs benefit from additional fridge time, but this dough just ended up being hard. The cookies still turned out great, though!

I make these every year, this recipe is wonderful! I reduce the candies to half for each cookie and push them on top of the cookie right when it comes out of the oven, this melts the candy for a better swirl.

Amazing recipe even when I replaced white flour with whole wheat. (Use 3/4 cup whole wheat for every 1 cup white).

Need to bake for longer than 10 minutes or cookies are too soft.
I found this recipe easy to follow and came out great! The flavor and softness are amazing!!! I will definitely be making this every year!

so I heavily tweaked the recipe. but holy fork balls these were so good. the tweaks I made: -subbed water for whipped cream (because I have it and it's going bad. probably didn't make much of a difference in the recipe) -melted 1/4 cup semi sweet mint chocolate w 1/4 cup andes mint chips (because I bought it last year on an after christmas on sale so I need to use that or else it will go bad) -added 1/4 andes mint chips + 3 drops peppermint extract to the cooled batter -rolled the dough (1tbsp each - I make a lot of small cookies) and made them into disks & put the remaining 1/4 cup of andes mint chocolates onto the surface of the disk. -fridge x1hr, then frozen (gotta start xmas cookies in november so you don't die in december getting them all done) -baked at 350F x13min its amazingly crunch on the edges and chewy inside 10/10!!!

I usually let it be in the fridge for at least over night. It is a bit of a pain to scoop and roll into balls after cooling down but it so so worth it. They are soooo good. Only suggestion is if you like a chew cookie take them out early

These have been my children’s favorite cookie for 20 years! Everyone I bake them for loves them! I let the dough sit in the fridge overnight, measure out the next day and bake. I also use the Andie’s Candies chips rather than the wrapped pieces, less waste, but you don’t get the pretty green swirl.

I started making this about two to three years ago for Christmas. It has now become one of my standard go tos for Christmas cookies. One loves them and they don't last long! Make sure that you allow the mint candy to sit on the hot cookie for about one minute at least before you try to spread it.
My daughter won the Christmas cookie contest with these! They are amazing!

Oh my gosh, these little devils are amazing! I followed the recipe as written and they turned out beautifully. The part that was the most fun was swirling those Andes mints around on the tops of the cookies. I’m including them on the cookie plates for my neighbors this Christmas and will most definitely make them again. Thank you!
I've been making these for years. They are always so successful and so yummy!
I loved them, but my kids did not. Easy recipe, but I found it hard to make the pretty swirls with the Andes mints on top.
